title: TP stability (multi-GPU) kickoff notes — Feb 2025
linked_artifacts: Linear: ENG-2406 (Collective timeouts + async error propagation)
Confluence: TP stability hangs — root causes & fix plan (serving runtime)
Confluence: ADR-0147 — TP collective timeouts & async error propagation
Confluence: Postmortem 2025-02-13 TP hang us-east Sev1
content:
Doc purpose
- Working kickoff notes for the TP stability initiative.
- This is NOT the final design doc. Expect rough hypotheses + TODOs.
- Canonical tracking: Linear ENG-2401. Canonical design: Confluence “TP stability hangs — root causes & fix plan” + ADR-0147.

Date / attendees
- Kickoff: 2025-02-17
- Attendees: Noah (runtime arch), Sofia (scheduling), Hiro (kernels/collectives), Grace/Yuki (kernel ICs), Marcus/Julian (scheduler ICs), Omar (observability), Sean/Rafael (SRE), Connor (releases), Sahana (CI/perf-canary), Dev/Owen (support escalation)

Why we’re doing this (problem framing)
- We have recurring customer-visible timeouts / stuck streams when tensor-parallel (TP) is enabled under sustained load.
- Failure mode is worse in multi-GPU nodes and large pools (Hosted high-load, Dedicated clusters with long-lived streams).
- Current handling keeps “stuck” TP groups alive; scheduler keeps routing new work to them; request-level timeouts become elevated 5xx/timeout rates.

What “good” looks like (high-level outcomes)
- No more silent stalls: async collective errors / comm failures surface quickly and deterministically.
- If a TP group loses forward progress, it is quarantined quickly and removed from scheduling.
- Oncall can immediately distinguish:
  (a) comm stall (collective latency spikes / NCCL error)
  (b) kernel stall (GPU stream stuck)
  (c) scheduler starvation / deadlock (barrier/cancel interactions)
- Reduced paging + faster mitigation playbook.

Constraints / non-goals (re-confirmed)
- Preserve latency and throughput; avoid global locks / heavy synchronization.
- No major refactor of model-parallel architecture; no new comm backend.
- Avoid watchdog false positives causing unnecessary resets.

Known symptom snapshots (from recent incidents + support)
- “Streaming hangs” at high concurrency: stream remains open, tokens stop; client eventually times out.
- Pool-level impact: a subset of TP worker groups appear “dead”; node remains allocated; capacity looks present but is unusable.
- Common traces/log patterns (informal):
  - collective call doesn’t return; no error returned
  - request canceled (client disconnect) while ranks are out-of-sync -> barrier waiting forever
  - rank-level skew: one rank advances step counter; others stay flat

Initial hypotheses (not exhaustive)
1) NCCL async error propagation gap
- We are not polling/observing NCCL async errors frequently enough; error only surfaces when the next collective is launched (or never).
- In some cases the kernel stream is waiting on an event tied to a failed comm op, and we never return control to check errors.

2) Scheduler + barrier/cancellation deadlock
- Request cancellation arrives mid-step; some ranks unwind, others still attempt to participate in barrier/collective.
- Barrier implementation assumes “all ranks are still alive + participating”, which is violated under streaming disconnects.
- Result: a “partial TP group” that cannot make forward progress.

3) Insufficient backpressure / fairness under mixed seq lengths
- Long sequences keep TP group busy; short requests stack behind; cancellations increase.
- Under overload, scheduler may push work into already degraded TP groups.

4) Watchdog missing or too coarse
- Node-level watchdog doesn’t map to TP group health.
- We need TP-group forward-progress detection + a clear quarantine + teardown policy.

5) Observability gaps
- We can’t quickly tell if a stall is comm vs kernel vs scheduler.
- Need per-rank progress + collective latency histograms + structured stall logs.

Decision points we need to make early
A) Failure domain: what do we “kill”?
- Options discussed:
  - Quarantine TP group and reset only that group (preferred), leaving process alive if possible.
  - Restart whole worker process.
  - Drain entire node.
- Tentative direction: quarantine at TP-group level, escalate to process restart if repeated triggers in a window.

B) Timeout semantics for collectives
- What is the timeout threshold? How do we set default vs per-deployment mode?
- When a timeout triggers, do we abort communicator? (Likely yes, but ensure we don’t wedge CUDA streams.)

C) What is “forward progress”?
- Candidate signals:
  - per-rank step counter increments
  - “tokens generated” counter increments
  - “collective completed” counter increments
  - time since last successful all-reduce/all-gather for active request

Owners / substreams (initial)
- Program mgmt / coordination: Talia
- Runtime architecture / integration glue: Noah
- Scheduler + TP lifecycle + cancellation semantics: Sofia
- Kernels + collectives hardening: Hiro
- Observability / metrics/logs + dashboard requirements: Omar + Allison (consult) + Sergio (impl)
- SRE guardrails, paging thresholds, rollout: Sean + Rafael
- Releases: Connor
- CI/perf-canary: Sahana
- Support escalations + external comms feedback: Dev + Owen

Execution plan (6–8 week target; dates rough)
Week 1–2: Triage + reproduction
- Consolidate incident evidence (Sev1 2025-02-13 + recent support tickets)
- Define stall taxonomy + “signature” mapping to likely root cause
- Build stress harness that can reproduce at least one signature reliably

Week 2–5: Fix implementation
- Scheduler: cancellation-safe barrier semantics; prevent deadlocks
- Collectives: async error checks, timeouts, error propagation to scheduler
- TP-group health model: states + quarantine + reset policy
- Backpressure / fairness tweaks if needed

Week 5–6: Validation + canary
- Perf regression gates (throughput/latency)
- Perf-canary nightly scenario; alert on watchdog triggers/stalls
- Targeted Hosted canary in high-load pool (us-east + one EU region)

Week 6–8: Rollout + follow-ups
- Dedicated opt-in + playbooks
- Documentation/runbooks + known-issues page update
- Track support tickets to closure; evaluate if any customer needs hotfix build

Concrete deliverables (checklist)
[ ] Stall taxonomy + mapping doc (what we think is happening)
[ ] Repro harness with knobs:
    - overload pattern (QPS ramp)
    - mixed sequence length distribution
    - forced rank delay (inject sleep / cuda sync)
    - forced cancellation mid-stream
    - optional forced NCCL error injection (where feasible)
[ ] Scheduler fixes:
    - cancellation semantics across ranks
    - barrier resilience (no “wait forever”)
    - don’t route new work to quarantined group
[ ] Collective hardening:
    - periodic async error check cadence
    - collective timeout handling
    - clear abort policy + surface to scheduler
[ ] Watchdog/quarantine:
    - define forward progress
    - sensitivity thresholds (avoid false positives)
    - metrics: triggers, quarantines, resets, repeated offenders
[ ] Observability pack:
    - per-rank progress counters
    - collective latency histogram by op type
    - structured logs for “comm stall”, “kernel stall”, “scheduler starvation” (best-effort)
    - dashboard panels + alerts with runbook links
[ ] Rollout checklist + rollback triggers
[ ] Release notes (runtime 1.19 patch/hotfix if needed)

Instrumentation requirements (minimum viable)
- Metrics
  - tp.rank.progress_step{model, tp_group_id, rank}
  - tp.collective.latency_ms{op_type, model, tp_group_id}
  - tp.watchdog.triggered_total{reason}
  - tp.group.quarantined_total{reason}
  - tp.group.reset_total{reason}
  - tp.scheduler.queue_depth{pool, model}
  - tp.scheduler.starvation_ms{tp_group_id}
- Logs (structured)
  - event=tp_collective_stall_detected
  - event=tp_rank_skew_detected
  - event=tp_group_quarantined
  - include: tp_group_id, rank (if applicable), last_progress_ts, current_request_id (if safe), model_version, node_id

Open questions / risks
- How do we safely teardown a wedged communicator without leaving CUDA streams stuck?
- How to avoid watchdog thrash (quarantine/reset loop) under temporary load spikes?
- What’s the clean rollback for Hosted? (feature flag? config-only?)
- Dedicated: do we need per-customer defaults (depending on GPU/driver)?
- Are there known driver/NCCL combinations where error propagation behaves differently?

Immediate next steps (48–72h)
- Noah + Sofia: write 1–2 page “TP group lifecycle + failure states” sketch (for alignment before coding).
- Hiro: propose async error check strategy + timeout thresholds candidates (tie to ADR-0147 draft).
- Omar + Rafael: draft metric names + alert thresholds strawman; share in #eng-sre thread for feedback.
- Sahana: start perf-canary job definition for “TP overload + forced cancel” scenario.
- Talia: convert this checklist into Linear sub-issues under ENG-2401; set weekly checkpoint cadence.

Notes from discussion (raw)
- Sean: biggest pain is not knowing whether to shift traffic vs drain node vs restart worker; we need a decisive signal + automated quarantine.
- Sofia: cancellation semantics currently too request-centric; needs group-aware unwind.
- Hiro: need to ensure we’re not blocking on an event recorded on a different stream that never completes after NCCL failure.
- Connor: if we target runtime 1.19.x hotfix, we need guardrails + opt-in initially; default-on can wait for the next minor.
- Dev: customers want a clear workaround today (timeouts/flags); support needs a single page to reference until the full fix ships.
